## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r nearest neighbor}
#Subset the integrated data by sample name

sample1 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "nonsmoker1")
sample2 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "nonsmoker2")
sample3 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "nonsmoker3")
sample4 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "smoker1")
sample5 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "copd1")
sample6 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "copd2")
sample7 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "copd3")

# Step 1 — extract coordinates for each
coords_subset1 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample1)
coords_subset2 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample2)
coords_subset3 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample3)
coords_subset4 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample4)
coords_subset5 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample5)
coords_subset6 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample6)
coords_subset7 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample7)

# Ensure rownames are set to the cell IDs
rownames(coords_subset1) <- coords_subset1$cell

# Identify B cells and AT2 cells based on sample1$celltype
b_spots   <- rownames(coords_subset1)[sample1$celltype[coords_subset1$cell] == "B cells"]
at2_spots <- rownames(coords_subset1)[sample1$celltype[coords_subset1$cell] == "AT2"]

# Subset the coordinates
coords_bcell <- coords_subset1[b_spots, c("x","y"), drop = FALSE]
coords_at2   <- coords_subset1[at2_spots, c("x","y"), drop = FALSE]

nn <- get.knnx(
  data  = as.matrix(coords_at2),    # reference points (AT2)
  query = as.matrix(coords_bcell),  # query points (B cells)
  k     = 1
)


# Distances from B cells to nearest AT2
distances_ns1 <- nn$nn.dist

summary(distances_ns1)
```
